I'll use my knowledge of chemistry to analyze each statement:

A. Alkali metals have a high ionization potential and a high electron affinity
Alkali metals (Group 1) actually have low ionization energies (not high) because they readily lose their single valence electron to form +1 ions. They also have low electron affinities because they don't tend to gain electrons. This statement is FALSE.

B. Halogens have a high ionization potential and a high electron affinity
Halogens (Group 17) have high ionization energies because they hold onto their electrons strongly. They also have high electron affinities because they readily accept an electron to complete their outer shell. This statement is TRUE.

C. In one period, the atomic radius increases from left to right
Across a period (left to right), the atomic radius actually decreases because the increasing nuclear charge pulls electrons closer to the nucleus while the number of electron shells remains the same. This statement is FALSE.

D. Metals tend to be on the right of the periodic table, nonmetals tend to be on the left
This is reversed. Metals are generally found on the left side of the periodic table, while nonmetals are on the right side. This statement is FALSE.

E. The electronegativity falls from right to left in one period
Electronegativity is the tendency of an atom to attract electrons. It increases from left to right across a period as nuclear charge increases. So electronegativity decreases (falls) from right to left. This statement is TRUE.

F. Within a group, the atomic radius increases
As you move down a group, new electron shells are added, which increases the atomic radius despite the increased nuclear charge. This statement is TRUE.

Based on my analysis, the correct answers are:
B. Halogens have a high ionization potential and a high electron affinity
E. The electronegativity falls from right to left in one period
F. Within a group, the atomic radius increases

Final Answer: [ANSWER]B,E,F[/ANSWER]
